label: Computer
description: A computer a program works on: a screen with a window manager, a terminal and a browser (Firefox), a mouse, a keyboard, and a shell. Every action node (Screenshot, Click, TypeText, RunCommand, ...) takes its `computer` output. Its home folder is a disk kept across `weft infra stop`, so a stopped computer keeps its work, and `weft infra terminate` deletes it. No credential is inside unless the program puts one there. If you want to get into it yourself (to look around, check a build, or let a person work in it), give it `sshKeys`: it then opens SSH to the install's own network, and `weft infra list-doors` prints the address to use as `ssh -p <port> user@<host>`; that is the way in for anything interactive, rather than streaming commands through RunCommand. One computer has one screen, so agents working at the same time each want a computer of their own (a `@per_instance` Computer gives each instance one), coordinating through a shared git repository. To have a model work it, include `__catalog/base_catalog/computer/agent.weft`, or build your own agent around `__catalog/base_catalog/computer/perform.weft` (copy either into your own `src/` and change it when your case differs). A browser wants about 1Gi of its `memory`.

inputs.name: screen
inputs.label: Screen size
inputs.description: Width and height of the screen in pixels, which is also the size of every screenshot. 1280x800 fits within every model vendor's image limits, so a coordinate a model reads off a screenshot is a real screen pixel.

inputs.name: packages
inputs.label: Extra packages
inputs.description: Debian packages to install at every start, separated by spaces. The machine already has Firefox, a terminal, git, curl and Python 3; anything else a program can also install itself with `sudo apt-get install` through RunCommand.

inputs.name: sshKeys
inputs.label: SSH keys
inputs.description: Public SSH keys allowed in as the computer's user, one per line (the lines of an `authorized_keys` file). Set, they open SSH to the install's own network (your machine on a local install, the install's private network on a cloud one; never the internet) and replace the computer's `~/.ssh/authorized_keys` at every start. Public keys are not secrets, so they can live in the program. Left out, the computer has no SSH.

inputs.name: disk
inputs.label: Home disk
inputs.description: Size of the disk holding the home folder, a number followed by Gi, Mi, G or M (`10Gi`).

outputs.name: computer
outputs.description: The computer's handle. Wire it into the `computer` input of every action node. Baked: made when the computer's infra is applied, so a run that reads only this output uses the saved handle and does not run this node.

then.message: Computer '{id}' has a `screen` it cannot read. Write the width and height in pixels, joined by x (1280x800).
Computer '{id}' has `packages` that are not Debian package names. Write the names separated by spaces (libreoffice gimp).
Computer '{id}' has a `disk` it cannot read. Write a number followed by Gi, Mi, G or M (10Gi).
Computer '{id}' has `sshKeys` that are not public SSH keys. Write one key per line, as in an authorized_keys file (ssh-ed25519 AAAA... you@laptop).
